operations.original: 1.1 Take the $C^1$ map $F$ constructed in [L1]. The construction gives a closed set $K\subseteq[0,1]$ and a $C^1$ function $g$ with $g'=0$ on $K$ and $g(K)=C$, the middle-thirds Cantor set, and sets $F(x,y)=g(x)+g(y)$. On $K\times K$ the derivative of $F$ is zero, so these points are critical. The same proof establishes $F(K\times K)=C+C=[0,2]$. [L1, given, choose]
operations.proposed: 1.1 By the existence assertion of [L1], fix $F\in C^1(\mathbb R^2,\mathbb R)$ whose critical-value set contains the entire interval $[0,2]$. This uses the supplied conclusion directly; the Cantor-sum construction establishing that conclusion is proved in the supplier. [L1, given, choose]
